I would like to begin by noting that this session has been convened in very specific circumstances so that the Assembly can address a complex and sensitive disciplinary matter as part of its governance and oversight role of the International Criminal Court. I trust that I can count on your cooperation to ensure that the Assembly can address the matter in a way that fully respects the privacy and rights of the persons involved, as well as the Court as an institution. Before we address the substantive issues, I would like to provide some practical information. We must also take some procedural decisions to ensure the smooth Conduct of the assembly proceedings. Pursuant to the decision of the Bureau at its 18th meeting on 8th of July, 2026, delegations are seated in the English alphabetical order. Due to the limited capacity of the room, 2 seats have been allocated for each state party. Other delegates are invited to take the seats reserved at the back of the room. Seats are also reserved at the back of the room for observer states, as well as other observers, participants, and invitees, in accordance with Rules 92, 93, and 94 of the Rules of Procedure. NGOs are invited to take their seats in the gallery. Distinguished delegates, in accordance with Article 112, Paragraph 1 of the Rome Statute, States that are not parties to the Statute but have signed either the Statute or the Final Act of the Rome Conference may participate as observers in the Assembly. Observer states are allowed to participate in the public deliberations of the Assembly but may not participate in the taking of decisions. States that are not parties to the Rome Statute and that have not signed the Final Act the Statute do not have observer status. Under Rule 94 of the Rules of Procedure, the President may invite those states to be present during the work of the Assembly, subject to approval from the Assembly. I note that at its 16th meeting on 17 June 2026, the Bureau decided to recommend that the special session be held in private pursuant to Rule 42, paragraph 1 of the Rules of Procedure of the Assembly of States Parties, in light of the exceptional circumstance of disciplinary proceedings against an elected official. For that reason, invitations to this session were not sent to States that are not parties to the Rome Statute and that have not signed the Final Act or the Rome Statute. In line with the recommendation of the Bureau, the programme of work for the special session provides for the plenary meetings to be held in private when the Assembly considers Agenda Item 7, disciplinary proceedings against an elected official.
